# Host agent

A host agent runs rimsky work on a developer's own machine. It reverses the usual direction: instead of rimsky dialing your service, your agent dials rimsky's host-agent proxy and holds one stream open. Rimsky then reaches your machine over that stream.

Rimsky ships a host agent. Implement this protocol yourself only when you need an agent rimsky's does not give you.

Proto file: `host_agent.proto`.

## The RPC

| RPC | Shape |
| --- | --- |
| `HostAgent.Connect(stream ClientFrame) → stream ServerFrame` | Bidirectional streaming |

`HostAgent` declares no `Capabilities` RPC. One stream carries everything.

## The frames

You send `ClientFrame`, a oneof over six bodies. The proxy sends `ServerFrame`, a oneof over six bodies. The pairs:

| You send | The proxy sends | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Register` | `RegisterAck` | Open the session |
| `HostAgentHeartbeat` | `HostAgentHeartbeatAck` | Keep the session alive |
| `SpawnAck` | `Spawn` | Start a local binary |
| `Reaped` | `Reap` | Stop a local binary |
| `DispatchFrame` | `DispatchFrame` | Carry protocol traffic in both directions |
| `LocalHttpForward` | `LocalHttpResponse` | Reach an HTTP endpoint through the proxy |

## Registering

Send `Register` as the very first frame. Any other first frame closes the stream with `InvalidArgument` and the message `first frame must be Register`.

`Register` fields:

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `api_key` | Your api-key plaintext, or the literal `anonymous`. Required. |
| `agent_label` | A human-readable name for this agent |
| `agent_version` | Your agent's version |
| `local_callback_base_url` | Where the proxy reaches your agent's HTTP callbacks |
| `routing_label` | A routing name to claim, for an anonymous agent |

The proxy verifies your key by calling `GET /v1/auth/whoami` on the control API with it as a bearer token, and routes work to you by the key id the control API reports. The literal `anonymous` sends the request unauthenticated, which works while the deployment is in anonymous mode.

The proxy fails closed. Without a control-API URL it refuses every registration. A key the control API rejects closes the stream with `Unauthenticated`.

`RegisterAck` returns:

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `proxy_version` | The proxy's protocol version |
| `displaced_prior` | Whether your registration displaced an earlier connection |
| `routing_identity` | The identity work is routed to you under |

An api-key registration displaces any earlier connection under the same key id, and `displaced_prior` says so. An anonymous registration works differently: it claims a routing label rather than displacing. Present a `routing_label` and the proxy rejects it with `AlreadyExists` when another connected anonymous agent already holds it. Omit it and the proxy assigns you a generated name, retrying up to 32 times before answering `ResourceExhausted`.

Send `Register` again on a live stream and the proxy ignores it.

## Heartbeats

Send `HostAgentHeartbeat` with `sent_at_unix_ms`. The proxy answers `HostAgentHeartbeatAck` with `received_at_unix_ms`. Keep sending them; when your stream drops, the proxy drops every spawn it was holding for you.

## Spawning

The proxy sends `Spawn` to start a binary on your machine.

`Spawn` fields:

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `spawn_id` | The id you answer with |
| `binding` | What to run |
| `cwd` | Working directory |
| `run_scope_id` | The execution context this spawn serves |
| `expected_protocols` | The protocols the spawned process should serve |
| `ready_timeout_seconds` | How long you may take to report ready |

`Binding` carries `path`, `args`, an `env` map, `cwd`, and its own `ready_timeout_seconds`.

Answer with `SpawnAck` carrying the same `spawn_id`, a `status` of `SPAWN_STATUS_READY` or `SPAWN_STATUS_FAILED`, a `capabilities` map from protocol name to advertised bytes, and an `error` on failure. `HostAgentError` carries a `class` and a `message`.

**Pick a free port, put it in the child's environment as `RIMSKY_AGENT_PORT`, and poll until the child's gRPC server answers there.** There is no port handshake back from the child. A binary that ignores the variable or binds elsewhere fails your readiness poll, and the dispatch that asked for it fails with `spawn_failed`.

The proxy sends `Reap` with a `spawn_id` and a `sigterm_grace_seconds` to stop a spawn. Answer `Reaped` with the same `spawn_id`, a `clean` boolean, and an `error` when the stop went badly.

## Dispatch frames

`DispatchFrame` carries protocol traffic in both directions over the one stream.

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `spawn_id` | Which spawned process this frame belongs to |
| `protocol` | The protocol name |
| `payload` | The serialized message |
| `stream_id` | Which logical stream within the spawn |
| `kind` | `DISPATCH_FRAME_KIND_DATA`, `_HALF_CLOSE`, or `_CANCEL` |
| `claim_producer_verb` | `_OPEN`, `_COMMIT`, `_ABANDON`, or `_RELEASE` |
| `rpc_method` | The method name |

Route an inbound frame to the named spawn's local gRPC server, and send the reply back as a `DispatchFrame` with the same `spawn_id` and `stream_id`.

## HTTP forwarding

Send `LocalHttpForward` when a spawned process needs to reach an HTTP endpoint the proxy can see. It carries `forward_id`, `method`, `url`, `body`, a `headers` map, and `spawn_id`. The proxy answers `LocalHttpResponse` with the same `forward_id`, a `status`, a `body`, and `headers`.

## What the proxy serves

The proxy is itself a rimsky peer. It serves `Executor`, `ExecutorObservability`, `ClaimProducer`, `ClaimProducerObservability`, and `LifecycleSubscriber` to the deployment, and translates each call into dispatch frames on your stream.

The proxy reads these environment variables:

| Variable | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `RIMSKY_PROXY_GRPC_PORT` | Agent-facing listener. Default 9090. |
| `RIMSKY_PROXY_PEER_GRPC_PORT` | Peer-facing mutual-TLS listener. Default 9091. |
| `RIMSKY_PROXY_TLS_CERT`, `RIMSKY_PROXY_TLS_KEY` | TLS for the agent-facing listener |
| `RIMSKY_CONTROL_API_URL` | Required. Where the proxy verifies your key. |
| `RIMSKY_CONTROL_API_TOKEN` | Token for the proxy's own control-API reads |
| `RIMSKY_CONTROL_API_CA` | CA bundle verifying an HTTPS control API |

Under `RIMSKY_PEER_AUTH=mtls` the proxy enrolls like any other peer service and serves the peer protocols on a separate mutual-TLS listener that requires client certificates from the deployment CA. The agent-facing listener then carries the host-agent protocol alone. Setting `RIMSKY_CONTROL_API_CA` alongside a non-HTTPS control-API URL is a startup error.

## Proving it

There is no conformance subcommand for the host-agent protocol. `rimsky conformance host-agent` answers `unknown subcommand`. Write your own tests against the frame contract above.
